summary: Two things in one submission. First, the coherence fix the previous turn could not make: the adverse-phase interpretation now records the knowledge entry it rests on at its exact revision, with the attribution limitation stated in the entry's own text, so the link between the two-gate behaviour and the run that exercised it is no longer implicit. Second, a probe that separates those two gates, because the earlier negative result could not: the isolated voter never raised its term, which is pre-vote holding it at the leader's own term, so the run confirmed the separation but left its cause entangled. The probe repeats the same adverse construction with PreVoteDisabled set on every node, which is a supported deployment choice, and records both whether a higher-term candidacy forms at all and whether any confirmation follows a competing leader. Native feedback from the local dry run, explicitly not retained evidence: with pre-vote off the candidacy did form in all twelve trials — the campaigner sat at terms three to five against a leader at two or three — and still no competing leader appeared during any confirmation window, with confirmations ending at the leader's lease in every trial. If the retained run reproduces that, the uniform-case separation rests on the peers' known-leader refusal together with their own timers rather than on pre-vote, and the defect's scope stays where the mixed-timer work put it: an inequality between a voter's election timeout and the leader's lease is still the only path in. I declared the overlap prediction as the comparison under test rather than assuming the negative, so the receipt will either return witnesses that the known-leader gate suffices on its own or, if an overlap appears, show that disabling pre-vote widens the defect beyond mixed timings.
